Subject: CareSync discovery — model recommendations & long-context Qs

Holly — great to meet you and the CareSync team this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so nothing gets lost.

TL;DR — recommended models and a focused long-context eval plan to validate summarization fidelity across 8k/32k windows.

Call summary:
- Use case: clinician note ingestion + patient timeline summarization for care ops (near real-time).
- Current note size: median ~2k tokens, 95th percentile ~18k tokens (bundle of encounter+attachments).
- Priority: high fidelity of clinical summarization (no hallucinations) and predictable latency for endpoint responses.

Our immediate recommendations:
1) Eval targets: 8k (fast path) and 32k (extended) model variants to measure truncation and prefix preservation.
2) Models to benchmark: redwood-ronin-8k, redwood-extended-32k (both quantized and FP16 baselines).
3) Prompts & prompts sets: we will share a prompt bank (structured system prompt + examples) tuned for extractive timeline + safety constraints.
4) Quality checks: ROUGE + targeted clinical slot-checks (meds, allergies, follow-ups) + human spot-checks for critical fields.

Concrete next steps (action items):
- I: Send a sample bundle from your PROD dev export (anonymized) — you mentioned 10-15 examples. Please drop to the evaluation email or the attached JSONL.
- Rishi: run a quick latency/throughput sanity run on redwood-ronin-8k vs extended-32k once we have the sample set (we'll provide a script).
- Marissa: propose an evaluation plan (benchmarks, acceptance thresholds, timeline) by EOD Wednesday.
- Holly: confirm whether PII/anonymization is complete for the samples and whether the legal team needs a data processing addendum before we ingest.

I attached a lightweight checklist (connor_long_context_eval_checklist.xlsx) that maps sample sizes to the eval matrix — should help prioritize. Also included a sample JSONL format we prefer (caresync_sample_notes_YYYYMMDD.jsonl).

Links referenced:
- Quick benchmarks: https://drive.redwood.com/benchmarks/long-context-template (we'll populate with your numbers)
- Prompt bank (preview): https://drive.redwood.com/prompts/clinical-timeline-v1

Expected timeline: initial sanity run in 48–72 hours after we receive the samples; full eval (human spot-check + metrics) in ~10 business days.

Feel free to correct any detail — happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up if you prefer a walkthrough of the checklist.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Connor — thanks for the clear recap and checklist. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) Sample files: we can provide 12 de-identified encounters (we'll scrub patient names, MRNs, and PHI per our DPA). Dropoff ETA end of day Tuesday.
2) Summarization fidelity: our biggest concern is loss of critical structured items (meds/allergies) when the context is long and the model resorts to higher-level summarization. We need a way to guarantee (or at least have a measurable threshold for) extractive accuracy for those fields.
3) Truncation behavior: when the model receives a 18k token note on an 8k model, what will fail? Do you suggest chunking+overlap or prefer the 32k variant for fidelity? We have latency constraints — 8k models are notably cheaper.
4) Security/compliance: Legal asked whether Redwood can run the eval in a private VPC; is that available for a short POC?

Quick answers on our side: we can share a single, annotated example that flags the critical slots we expect preserved. Also looping in our evaluation lead (evaluation-team@caresync.com) for acceptance criteria.

Holly Kramer
Head of Product | CareSync
holly@caresync.com

Holly / Connor — quick technical follow-up and suggested eval knobs.

Thanks for the sample plan, Connor. A few notes from the infra/eval side that should help decide 8k vs 32k: 

- Truncation behavior: an 8k serving model will keep the most recent 8k tokens (by default). For clinical timelines where critical data may be earlier in the note, chunking with overlap (e.g., 4k stride) and a downstream merge-step (extract slots, then stitch) typically preserves structured fields but costs more in tokens and latency.
- 32k variant trade-offs: extended-window models avoid chunk/reassemble complexity and reduce extraction error for fields that appear earlier in documents, but they increase per-request memory and slightly higher p99 latency.
- Recommendation for POC: run both in parallel on 12 samples. Measurement plan:
  * Extraction recall for meds/allergies/follow-ups (binary pass/fail per slot).
  * Summarization ROUGE-L and a small human-grade fidelity score (0-5) for critical content.
  * Cost per successful extraction (tokens + compute time).

Links & artifacts I uploaded for your review:
- Quick model comparison script: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/long-context-evals/DEAL-2027-0342/run_compare.sh
- Baseline prompts (clinical timeline v1): https://drive.redwood.com/prompts/clinical-timeline-v1

A few practical suggestions to speed iteration:
- If you must prioritize latency/cost, begin with redwood-ronin-8k + chunk/merge; flag failure modes and only promote to extended-32k for samples that fail extraction thresholds.
- We'll supply a patched inference profile that caches KV prefixes across similar documents to reduce repeated token cost for recurring header blocks (helpful if templates repeat).

I can run the initial sanity runs in our sandbox (not production) if CareSync confirms DPA approval for the sample set. If you need a VPC for the POC, that is possible — I will loop our solutions engineer and provide the private endpoint details (this typically adds 1–2 business days to the setup).

- Rishi

Holly — thanks for the quick turnaround and for confirming the sample delivery. Finalizing logistic notes and proposed timeline: 

1) Sample ingestion: please upload the 12 de-identified JSONL examples to the Drive link I shared (or reply with a secure shared S3/transfer link). We'll validate format by EOD Thursday.
2) Sandbox runs: Rishi will kick off both redwood-ronin-8k (chunk+merge) and redwood-extended-32k (single-pass) on the set the morning after validation; expect preliminary metrics within 48 hours.
3) VPC option: yes, we can run the POC in a private VPC. I'll have our solutions engineer (cc'd here) reach out to your infra lead; set expectation +1–2 business days for the endpoint.
4) Acceptance criteria (proposal):
   - Extraction recall >= 95% for meds and allergies across the sample set, OR
   - If recall <95% on 8k+chunk, then move failing classes to extended-32k for production.

Next meeting suggestion: 30-min sync on Friday to review preliminary numbers (Connor + Rishi + Holly + CareSync evaluation lead). I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm times.

Thanks again — excited to get this moving.

Connor
